topics.subject: cia-2-2025-26:de
topics.title: TTL NAND gate
topics.brief: A TTL NAND gate uses bipolar transistors. Its output is LOW only when all inputs are HIGH.
topics.hinglish: NAND mein sirf saare inputs 1 hone par output 0 hota hai.
points: Input stage: a multi-emitter transistor senses the inputs.
If any input is LOW, the phase-splitter is off; the pull-down is off and the output goes HIGH.
If all inputs are HIGH, the phase-splitter conducts; the pull-down turns on and the output is LOW.
In an exam, draw the circuit from your class notes, label input, phase-splitter and totem-pole stages, then explain both cases.
topics.question: Explain the operation of a two-input TTL NAND gate with its truth table.
steps: Write the NAND expression: Y = NOT(A · B).
For 00, 01 and 10, at least one LOW input keeps the output HIGH.
For 11, the pull-down transistor conducts and output becomes LOW.
State that TTL uses bipolar transistors and label the three functional stages in your circuit.
topics.mcq: For a two-input NAND gate, which input gives output 0?
topics.explanation: NAND is the complement of AND; only 1 AND 1 is 1.

topics.subject: cia-2-2025-26:de
topics.title: Noise margin & logic levels
topics.brief: Noise margin is the noise voltage a logic signal can tolerate while still being read correctly.
topics.hinglish: Signal mein kitna unwanted voltage add ho sakta hai bina 0/1 galat padhe—ye noise margin hai.
points: VOH(min) and VOL(max) describe guaranteed output levels.
VIH(min) and VIL(max) describe accepted input levels.
High noise margin: NMH = VOH(min) − VIH(min).
Low noise margin: NML = VIL(max) − VOL(max). Use the actual device specifications.
topics.recall: NMH = VOH − VIH; NML = VIL − VOL
topics.question: Given VOH = 2.4 V, VIH = 2.0 V, VIL = 0.8 V and VOL = 0.4 V, find both noise margins.
steps: Identify the guaranteed HIGH output and minimum HIGH input.
Both states tolerate 0.4 V of adverse noise under these specified limits.
topics.mcq: Which expression gives the LOW noise margin?
topics.explanation: LOW output can rise from VOL(max) to VIL(max) before crossing the guaranteed LOW limit.

topics.subject: cia-2-2025-26:de
topics.title: Delay, fan-in & fan-out
topics.brief: Propagation delay measures switching time. Fan-in counts gate inputs; fan-out measures how many loads an output can drive.
topics.hinglish: Fan-in = gate ke inputs. Fan-out = output kitne gate inputs ko safely drive kare.
points: Average propagation delay: tp = (tPLH + tPHL) / 2.
For a DC current estimate, fan-out = min(|IOH/IIH|, |IOL/IIL|), rounded down.
Fan-in and fan-out are different specifications.
Capacitance and frequency can further limit practical fan-out.
topics.question: A gate has tPLH = 8 ns, tPHL = 12 ns; HIGH-state fan-out is 20 and LOW-state fan-out is 10. Find delay and usable DC fan-out.
steps: Average the two delays: (8 + 12)/2 = 10 ns.
Compare the two current-based load limits.
Choose the smaller limit: min(20,10) = 10.
Answer: average delay 10 ns; DC fan-out 10 loads, subject to timing limits.
topics.mcq: If HIGH fan-out is 16 and LOW fan-out is 10, the DC fan-out is:
topics.explanation: The output must satisfy both HIGH and LOW loading limits.

topics.subject: cia-2-2025-26:de
topics.title: Tri-state TTL & shared buses
topics.brief: A tri-state output has three states: logic 0, logic 1 and high impedance Z. Z disconnects the output electrically from the bus.
topics.hinglish: Z ka matlab third logic value nahi—output bus ko drive hi nahi kar raha.
points: An enable input controls whether the gate drives the bus.
When disabled, the output is high impedance.
Shared buses require only one driver enabled at a time.
Two active drivers with opposite levels can cause bus contention.
topics.question: Why are tri-state buffers used on a shared data bus?
steps: Several devices are connected to the same bus wires.
Enable only the device that should transmit; put other outputs in Z.
The enabled device drives 0 or 1 without fighting the other devices.
If opposite outputs drive together, contention can cause excess current and invalid data.
topics.mcq: A disabled tri-state output is:
topics.explanation: Z means the output is effectively disconnected.

topics.subject: cia-2-2025-26:de
topics.title: TTL, ECL & CMOS comparison
topics.brief: Logic families differ in transistor technology, switching behavior, power and input thresholds.
topics.hinglish: Family comparison mein technology, speed, power aur noise immunity likho; exact values series par depend karti hain.
points: TTL uses bipolar transistors; traditional TTL has moderate power consumption.
ECL uses non-saturating differential bipolar operation for fast switching, usually with substantial static power.
CMOS uses complementary MOS transistors; ideal static power is low, while switching power rises with frequency and capacitance.
Do not claim every CMOS family is slower than every TTL family: compare named series and datasheets.
topics.recall: CMOS switching power ≈ α C V² f
topics.question: Compare TTL, ECL and CMOS using four meaningful parameters.
steps: Identify technology: bipolar TTL; bipolar differential ECL; complementary MOS CMOS.
Explain ECL speed through avoidance of transistor saturation.
Compare power: traditional ECL relatively high static power; CMOS low ideal static power with frequency-dependent switching losses.
Discuss input levels/noise margin and supply compatibility; these depend on the actual series.
topics.mcq: ECL is fast mainly because its transistors:
topics.explanation: Avoiding saturation reduces charge-storage switching delays.

topics.subject: cia-2-2025-26:de
topics.title: TTL–CMOS interfacing
topics.brief: Interfacing requires compatible voltage levels and sufficient current drive in both logic states.
topics.hinglish: Sirf supply same hone se connection safe nahi; HIGH/LOW limits aur current bhi match hone chahiye.
points: Check VOH(driver) ≥ VIH(receiver).
Check VOL(driver) ≤ VIL(receiver).
Check output current can supply the receiver load.
At 5 V, a TTL HIGH is not necessarily enough for a standard HC CMOS input; TTL-compatible HCT or a suitable translator can help.
topics.question: A TTL output guarantees VOH = 2.4 V. A CMOS input needs VIH ≥ 3.5 V. Is direct HIGH-level interfacing guaranteed?
steps: Write the compatibility requirement: VOH(min) ≥ VIH(min).
Substitute: 2.4 ≥ 3.5 is false.
The connection is not guaranteed to register HIGH.
Use an appropriate TTL-compatible input family or level translator; also verify LOW level and current limits.
topics.mcq: Which condition is needed for a valid HIGH connection?
topics.explanation: The minimum guaranteed HIGH output must meet the receiver HIGH threshold.

topics.subject: cia-2-2025-26:de
topics.title: Memory elements, SRAM & DRAM
topics.brief: Memory stores bits. SRAM uses bistable cells; DRAM stores charge and requires refresh.
topics.hinglish: SRAM state ko hold karta hai; DRAM capacitor charge ko refresh karna padta hai.
points: A latch or flip-flop stores one bit of state.
SRAM retains data while powered without periodic refresh; it is commonly used for cache.
DRAM needs refresh and offers high density; it is commonly used for main memory.
Both SRAM and DRAM are volatile.
topics.question: Compare SRAM and DRAM on storage, refresh, density and application.
steps: SRAM: a bistable transistor cell stores each bit. DRAM: charge on a capacitor stores each bit.
SRAM does not need refresh; DRAM needs periodic refresh.
DRAM usually offers higher density and lower cost per bit; SRAM is commonly faster.
Examples: SRAM cache; DRAM main memory. Both lose data without power.
topics.mcq: Which memory requires refresh?
topics.explanation: Capacitor charge leaks, so DRAM cells need refresh.

topics.subject: cia-2-2025-26:de
topics.title: ROM types & memory organization
topics.brief: A memory organization gives the number of words and bits in each word. ROM-family technologies retain information without power.
topics.hinglish: Address lines words select karti hain; data lines ek word ke bits batati hain.
points: A memory with 2^n words needs n address lines.
Total capacity = number of words × bits per word.
PROM: programmable once; EPROM: UV erasable; EEPROM: electrically erasable.
Flash is electrically erased in blocks; read-only in ROM does not mean every ROM-family chip can never be programmed.
topics.question: Find address lines, data lines and capacity of a 4K × 8 memory.
steps: 4K = 4096 = 2^12 words, so 12 address lines are required.
Each word has 8 bits, so there are 8 data lines.
Capacity = 4096 × 8 = 32768 bits.
This equals 4096 bytes = 4 KiB.
topics.mcq: An 8K × 16 memory needs how many address lines?

topics.subject: cia-2-2025-26:de
topics.title: PLDs, PLA, PAL & FPGA
topics.brief: Programmable logic devices implement Boolean functions using configurable logic and connections.
topics.hinglish: Hardware ka logic configure karte hain; FPGA ek normal CPU instruction sequence jaisa concept nahi hai.
points: PLA: programmable AND and OR arrays.
PAL: typically programmable AND array with a fixed OR array.
FPGA: configurable logic blocks, lookup tables, routing and I/O; many include dedicated memory and arithmetic resources.
A lookup table stores the truth-table output for each combination of its input bits.
topics.question: Explain how an FPGA lookup table implements a Boolean function.
steps: List the truth-table output for every input combination.
Treat the k inputs as an address into a 2^k-entry table.
Store the required output bit at each address.
Connect LUTs using configurable routing for larger functions; use registers when state is needed.
topics.mcq: A 3-input LUT representing one output needs:
topics.explanation: Three inputs have 2^3 = 8 combinations.

topics.subject: cia-2-2025-26:de
topics.title: Logic implementation using PLDs
topics.brief: Implement a sum-of-products expression by generating product terms and connecting them to outputs.
topics.hinglish: Pehle Boolean expression simplify karo; phir AND terms banao aur OR output se jodo.
points: Write the function and simplify if possible.
List distinct product terms across outputs.
Choose the required true or complemented literals in the AND array.
Connect product terms to OR outputs and verify the truth table.
topics.recall: F = A̅B + AC → two product terms
topics.question: Implement F(A,B,C) = A̅B + AC using a PLA.
steps: Generate complemented input A̅ alongside A, B and C.
Program AND term P1 = A̅B and term P2 = AC.
Program the OR output F = P1 + P2.
Check: if A=0, F=B; if A=1, F=C. This verifies all input cases by splitting on A.
topics.mcq: For F = A̅B + AC, the listed SOP requires:
topics.explanation: The terms A̅B and AC are combined by OR.

topics.subject: cia-2-2025-26:de
topics.title: Boolean algebra, canonical SOP & POS
topics.brief: Boolean algebra represents switching logic using AND, OR and complement. Canonical forms contain every input variable in each term.
topics.hinglish: SOP mein AND terms ko OR karo; POS mein OR terms ko AND karo.
points: De Morgan: (AB)̅ = A̅+B̅ and (A+B)̅ = A̅B̅.
Absorption: A+AB=A; duality swaps AND/OR and 0/1.
A minterm is 1 for exactly one input row; a maxterm is 0 for exactly one row.
Canonical SOP lists rows with output 1; canonical POS lists rows with output 0.
topics.recall: F=Σm(1,3) = B for two inputs A,B
topics.question: Express F(A,B)=Σm(1,3) in canonical SOP and simplify.
steps: Row 1 is A=0,B=1 → A̅B.
Row 3 is A=1,B=1 → AB.
F=A̅B+AB=B(A̅+A).
Since A̅+A=1, F=B.
topics.mcq: Which is De Morgan’s complement of AB?
topics.explanation: Complementing an AND changes it to OR and complements both operands.

topics.subject: cia-2-2025-26:de
topics.title: K-maps, don’t-cares & Quine–McCluskey
topics.brief: Minimization combines adjacent binary terms that differ in one bit.
topics.hinglish: Groups powers of 2 mein banao. Don’t-care ko tabhi use karo jab expression chhota ho.
points: K-map cells use Gray-code order, and opposite edges are adjacent.
Group 1s for SOP; group 0s for POS. Groups may overlap and must have size 1,2,4,8,…
For 5–6 variables use multiple linked maps; corresponding cells across maps are adjacent.
Quine–McCluskey groups minterms by number of 1s, combines one-bit differences, then selects prime implicants. XOR/XNOR patterns may be recognized after checking the truth table.
topics.recall: A variable that changes within a group disappears
topics.question: Minimize F(A,B,C)=Σm(0,1,2,3) using a K-map.
steps: These four cells form a group with A=0 fixed.
B and C both vary and are eliminated.
Therefore F=A̅. Verify all four selected minterms share A=0.
topics.mcq: A valid K-map group can contain:
topics.explanation: Group sizes must be powers of two.

topics.subject: cia-2-2025-26:de
topics.title: Binary codes & code conversion
topics.brief: Codes assign bit patterns to numbers or symbols. BCD encodes each decimal digit separately; Gray code changes one bit between adjacent values.
topics.hinglish: Decimal 12 ka BCD 0001 0010 hai, normal binary 1100.
points: Weighted codes assign positional weights; 8421 BCD represents decimal digits 0–9.
Binary-to-Gray: keep the MSB; XOR each pair of adjacent binary bits.
Gray-to-binary: keep the MSB; successive binary bits are previous binary XOR current Gray.
Write a conversion truth table, then simplify each output function for a code-converter circuit.
topics.question: Convert binary 1011 to Gray code and back.
steps: Keep first bit 1.
Adjacent XOR values are 1⊕0=1, 0⊕1=1, 1⊕1=0; Gray=1110.
Decode: first binary bit 1; then 1⊕1=0, 0⊕1=1, 1⊕0=1.
Recovered binary is 1011.
topics.mcq: 8421 BCD for decimal 12 is:
topics.explanation: BCD encodes the digits 1 and 2 independently.

topics.subject: cia-2-2025-26:de
topics.title: Adders, subtractors & BCD addition
topics.brief: Arithmetic circuits combine bits with carry or borrow signals.
topics.hinglish: Full adder mein third input carry-in hota hai.
points: Half adder: S=A⊕B, C=AB; full adder: S=A⊕B⊕Cin, Cout=AB+ACin+BCin.
Half subtractor: D=A⊕B, Borrow=A̅B; full subtractor also accepts borrow-in.
Ripple/parallel addition chains carry stages; serial addition reuses arithmetic hardware over time.
BCD addition needs +0110 correction when a digit result exceeds 9 or produces a carry.
topics.question: Add BCD digits 7 and 8 with correction.
steps: 1111 is not a valid BCD digit, so add 0110.
Carry 1 is the tens digit; result 0001 0101 represents 15.
topics.mcq: A half adder carry output is:
topics.explanation: A carry occurs only when both one-bit inputs are 1.

topics.subject: cia-2-2025-26:de
topics.title: MUX, DEMUX, encoders & decoders
topics.brief: Selection and coding circuits route data or translate between binary codes and active lines.
topics.hinglish: MUX many-to-one; DEMUX one-to-many. Encoder aur decoder reverse roles hain.
points: A 2^n-to-1 MUX needs n select lines; it can implement Boolean functions.
A decoder maps an n-bit input to up to 2^n outputs; an encoder produces a code for an active input.
Priority encoders define which input wins when several are active.
Code converters and seven-segment drivers use truth tables; multiplexed displays activate digits in rapid sequence.
topics.question: Implement F(A,B,C)=Σm(1,2,6,7) using a 4:1 MUX with selectors A,B.
steps: For AB=00, outputs at C=0,1 are 0,1, so I0=C.
For AB=01, outputs are 1,0, so I1=C̅.
For AB=10, outputs are 0,0, so I2=0.
For AB=11, outputs are 1,1, so I3=1. Connect these data inputs.
topics.mcq: An 8:1 multiplexer requires how many select inputs?
topics.explanation: 2³=8 choices.

topics.subject: cia-2-2025-26:de
topics.title: Comparators, parity, barrel shifter & ALU
topics.brief: Combinational systems can compare values, detect parity, shift words and select arithmetic or logical operations.
topics.hinglish: ALU operation select karta hai; parity error detect kar sakti hai, generally correct nahi.
points: A magnitude comparator produces A>B, A=B and A<B outputs.
XOR reduction gives oddness of the number of 1 bits; a parity bit enforces even or odd total parity.
A barrel shifter shifts a whole word by a selected number of positions combinationally.
An ALU combines arithmetic and logic functions with operation selection and status flags.
topics.recall: Even parity bit = XOR of data bits
topics.question: Find the even-parity bit for data 1011 and explain its limitation.
steps: 1011 contains three 1 bits, which is odd.
Append parity bit 1 to make four 1s in total.
At the receiver, XOR of all transmitted bits should be 0.
An even number of bit flips can leave parity unchanged, so simple parity does not detect every error.
topics.mcq: Simple parity always detects:
options: Any odd number of bit flips
topics.explanation: An odd number of flips reverses parity.

topics.subject: cia-2-2025-26:de
topics.title: SR, JK, edge-triggered & master–slave flip-flops
topics.brief: Sequential circuits store state; flip-flops update on a clock event.
topics.hinglish: Latch level-sensitive, flip-flop normally edge-triggered.
points: For a NOR SR latch, S=R=1 is the forbidden condition; NAND active-low versions use a different input convention.
JK: 00 hold,01 reset,10 set,11 toggle; Qnext=JQ̅+K̅Q.
A level-sensitive JK can race when J=K=1 and the clock pulse is too long.
Master–slave or edge-triggered arrangements control when state changes; respect setup and hold times.
topics.question: A JK flip-flop starts at Q=0. Find Q after three active edges with J=K=1.
steps: At the first edge, toggle 0→1.
At the second edge, toggle 1→0.
At the third edge, toggle 0→1.
Final output is 1; the frequency is divided by two for steady toggling.
topics.mcq: JK input 00 causes:
topics.explanation: Both control inputs inactive preserve the previous state.

topics.subject: cia-2-2025-26:de
topics.title: Counters, shift registers & pulse generation
topics.brief: Counters follow state sequences; shift registers move stored bits between stages.
topics.hinglish: Ripple counter mein delay stages se accumulate hota hai; synchronous mein common clock hoti hai.
points: Ripple counters clock stages from preceding outputs; synchronous counters share a clock.
A mod-N counter needs at least ceil(log₂N) flip-flops, with unused states handled.
Shift registers support serial/parallel conversion, delay and ring/Johnson sequences.
LFSRs use XOR feedback for pseudorandom sequences; maximal length requires suitable taps and a non-locking seed.
topics.question: How many flip-flops are needed for a mod-10 counter? Explain a practical design check.
steps: Find the smallest n with 2^n≥10.
2³=8 is too small, while 2⁴=16 suffices.
Use four flip-flops and define states for 0 through 9.
Arrange reset/next-state behavior so unused states 10–15 recover rather than lock up.
topics.mcq: A 4-stage maximal-length binary LFSR has nonzero period:
topics.explanation: The all-zero state is excluded, leaving 2⁴−1 states.

topics.subject: cia-2-2025-26:de
topics.title: FSMs, ASM charts & synchronous design
topics.brief: A finite state machine defines outputs and next state from its current state and inputs.
topics.hinglish: Moore output state par; Mealy output state aur input dono par depend.
points: Write the specification, identify states and draw transitions with input conditions.
Build a state table, assign binary codes, choose flip-flops and derive next-state/output logic.
ASM charts separate state boxes, decision boxes and conditional output boxes.
Check reset, unreachable states and behavior on every clock event; pulse generators and controllers are standard applications.
topics.question: Design a two-state Moore machine that toggles output whenever input x=1 at a clock edge.
steps: Define S0 with y=0 and S1 with y=1; reset to S0.
For x=0, stay in the current state. For x=1, transition to the other state.
Encode S0=0,S1=1, yielding D=Q⊕x and y=Q.
Implement one D flip-flop plus XOR; test x=0,1 sequences and reset.
topics.mcq: A Moore machine output depends directly on:
topics.explanation: Outputs are associated with states.

topics.subject: cia-2-2025-26:de
topics.title: VLSI flow, Y-chart, FPGA & ASIC
topics.brief: VLSI development transforms a specification into a verified implementation. The Y-chart relates behavioral, structural and physical views.
topics.hinglish: Simulation behavior check karti hai; synthesis hardware structure banata hai.
points: Entry can be schematic, FSM or HDL. Verify behavior before synthesis.
Synthesis produces a netlist; physical implementation includes placement, routing and timing checks.
ASIC flow continues through sign-off, fabrication and testing; FPGA flow maps to programmable resources and produces a configuration bitstream.
Y-chart axes: behavioral (what), structural (components) and physical/geometrical (where), at several abstraction levels.
topics.recall: Specification → model → verify → synthesize → implement → validate
topics.question: Differentiate FPGA and ASIC development using two applications.
steps: FPGA maps a design to pre-existing configurable logic, enabling reprogramming and fast prototyping.
ASIC implements a custom fabricated circuit with significant upfront design/manufacturing cost.
Use an FPGA for a changing prototype or specialized low-volume processing system.
A stable high-volume function may justify ASIC optimization; compare cost, power, speed and flexibility rather than claiming one is always better.
topics.mcq: The Y-chart’s three domains are:
topics.explanation: The domains describe function, architecture and physical realization.

topics.subject: cia-2-2025-26:de
topics.title: VHDL entities, types, objects & modeling
topics.brief: VHDL describes hardware interfaces and behavior. An entity declares ports; an architecture describes implementation.
topics.hinglish: VHDL software ki tarah sequential program nahi; concurrent hardware describe karta hai.
points: std_logic includes 0,1,X,Z and other simulation states; std_logic_vector is an array, not automatically a number.
Signals represent connections; variables inside processes update immediately, while signal assignments schedule updates.
Dataflow uses concurrent assignments; behavioral uses processes; structural instantiates and connects components.
Use ieee.numeric_std and signed/unsigned for portable arithmetic.
topics.question: Give a dataflow description of a two-input AND gate.
steps: Declare ieee.std_logic_1164 and an entity with two inputs and one output.
Use architecture dataflow of the entity.
A concurrent assignment y <= a and b describes the gate.
Simulate input combinations 00,01,10,11 and expect 0,0,0,1.
topics.mcq: Which VHDL construct declares the external ports?
topics.explanation: The entity defines the design interface.

topics.subject: cia-2-2025-26:de
topics.title: VHDL combinational & sequential circuits
topics.brief: A complete combinational process assigns every output for every path; a clocked process models state.
topics.hinglish: Missing assignment se unintended latch infer ho sakta hai.
points: Use process(all) in VHDL-2008 or a complete sensitivity list for combinational logic.
A 4:1 MUX can be composed from three 2:1 MUX components for structural modeling.
Use rising_edge(clk) to describe a positive-edge register; explicitly specify reset behavior.
Simulation testbenches apply input stimulus and assertions; synthesis accepts only a hardware-realizable subset.
topics.question: Describe an enabled register with synchronous reset.
steps: At each rising edge, first check reset.
If reset=1, set stored q to 0.
Otherwise, if enable=1, load d; if enable=0, retain q.
The ordering gives reset priority over loading and changes q only at clock edges.
topics.mcq: Incomplete output assignments in combinational VHDL may infer:
topics.explanation: Retaining the previous value requires storage.

topics.subject: cia-2-2025-26:cpp
topics.title: Generic functions & type deduction
topics.brief: A function template describes one algorithm for multiple compatible types. The compiler instantiates it for the types used.
topics.hinglish: Logic ek baar likho; int ya double ke liye compiler suitable version banata hai.
points: Use template <typename T> before a function.
Type deduction usually determines T from arguments.
Operations inside the template must be valid for the selected type.
For one T parameter, mixed arguments such as int and double can fail deduction; explicitly select a common type when appropriate.
topics.recall: template <typename T> T maximum(T a, T b)
topics.question: Write a function template to return the larger of two values, and apply it to int and double.
steps: Declare a type parameter T using template <typename T>.
Return a > b ? a : b, with return type T.
Call maximum(3,7), which deduces T as int and returns 7.
Call maximum(2.5,1.2), which deduces double and returns 2.5.
topics.mcq: maximum(2, 3.5) with a single parameter type T normally:
topics.explanation: Use maximum<double>(2,3.5) or a template designed for distinct types.

topics.subject: cia-2-2025-26:cpp
topics.title: Generic classes & applying templates
topics.brief: A class template describes a family of classes whose data or behavior depends on a type parameter.
topics.hinglish: Box<int> aur Box<double> same blueprint se bane alag class types hain.
points: Put template <typename T> before the class definition.
Use T for data members, arguments or return types.
Instantiate with a concrete type, such as Box<int>.
Templates support reuse with compile-time type checking, but unsupported operations fail at instantiation.
topics.recall: Box<int> and Box<double> are distinct types
topics.question: Create a generic Box class that stores a value and returns it.
steps: Declare template <typename T> class Box.
Store a T data member; initialize it in the constructor.
Provide T get() const to return the stored value.
Instantiate Box<int> a(10); and Box<double> b(2.5);.
topics.mcq: Box<int> and Box<double> are:
topics.explanation: Each type argument generates a distinct class specialization.

topics.subject: cia-2-2025-26:cpp
topics.title: typename, export & template power
topics.brief: typename introduces a type parameter or disambiguates a dependent type. export has different historical and modern meanings.
topics.hinglish: Syllabus ka old export template aur modern module export alag concepts hain.
points: template <class T> and template <typename T> both introduce a type parameter.
In dependent contexts, typename C::value_type tells the compiler the dependent name is a type.
Historical export template supported separately defined templates; that feature was removed in C++11.
C++20 uses export with modules. Do not present old export template examples as modern executable code.
Advantages: reusable type-safe algorithms; trade-offs: compilation time, diagnostics and possible code size.
topics.question: Explain typename and the historical export keyword in templates.
steps: Show template <typename T> and explain that T represents a type.
Show typename C::value_type for a nested type that depends on C.
Explain that old exported templates attempted to separate a template definition from use.
Add the version distinction: old feature removed in C++11; modern export belongs to modules.
topics.mcq: In typename C::value_type, typename indicates:
topics.explanation: It disambiguates a dependent name as a type.

topics.subject: cia-2-2025-26:cpp
topics.title: try, throw & catch fundamentals
topics.brief: Exception handling transfers control from a throw to the nearest matching active handler.
topics.hinglish: try mein risky work, throw se error signal, catch mein handling. Throw ke baad try ka remaining code skip hota hai.
points: Place operations that may throw inside try.
throw creates or propagates an exception.
The first matching catch handles the exception; normal flow continues after the handler.
Automatic objects are destroyed while unwinding toward a matching handler. Use RAII for cleanup.
topics.question: Trace a division-by-zero check using a standard exception.
steps: Check b == 0 before dividing. Integer division by zero is not automatically a catchable C++ exception.
Throw std::invalid_argument with a meaningful message.
Catch const std::exception& and display what().
For b=0, print the message; for b≠0, perform division normally.
topics.mcq: What happens immediately after throw inside a try block?
topics.explanation: The rest of the throwing path is skipped as exception propagation begins.

topics.subject: cia-2-2025-26:cpp
topics.title: Derived exceptions & handler order
topics.brief: Catch derived exception classes before their base class, so specific handlers can be selected.
topics.hinglish: Parent catch pehle rakhoge to child exception bhi wahi pakad lega. Specific pehle, general baad mein.
points: A handler for a public unambiguous base class can match a derived exception.
Handlers are considered in source order.
Catch by const reference to avoid slicing and unnecessary copies.
Place catch(...) last, because it matches any exception.
topics.question: Why should invalid_argument be caught before std::exception?
steps: std::invalid_argument derives through std::logic_error from std::exception.
A catch(const std::exception&) can match invalid_argument too.
If placed first, it handles the exception and the later specific catch is not selected.
Put invalid_argument first, followed by std::exception, for specific then general handling.
topics.mcq: Which catch should normally appear first?
topics.explanation: A more specific handler belongs before the general base handler.

topics.subject: cia-2-2025-26:cpp
topics.title: Rethrowing & exception options
topics.brief: Multiple handlers, catch-all handlers, nested try blocks and rethrowing support different recovery paths.
topics.hinglish: throw; current exception ko original type ke saath dobara bhejta hai.
points: Use catch(...) for a final generic handler.
Use throw; inside an active handler to rethrow the current exception.
throw e; throws a new exception from the expression and can slice a derived object.
An outer handler can deal with a rethrown exception after local logging or cleanup.
topics.question: Explain how an inner catch can log an error and let an outer catch handle it.
steps: Place an inner try/catch inside an outer try.
When the inner operation throws, the inner handler logs the problem.
Use bare throw; in that handler to rethrow the current exception.
The outer matching handler receives it; the original dynamic exception type is preserved.
topics.mcq: Which statement correctly rethrows the active exception?
topics.explanation: Bare throw rethrows the current exception when a handler is active.

topics.subject: cia-2-2025-26:cpp
topics.title: terminate() & noexcept
topics.brief: std::terminate is invoked when exception handling cannot continue safely, including no matching handler or an exception escaping a noexcept function.
topics.hinglish: terminate recovery mechanism nahi hai; program ko end karta hai.
points: An uncaught exception can invoke std::terminate.
An exception escaping a noexcept function invokes std::terminate.
A destructor throwing during stack unwinding can also lead to termination.
std::set_terminate changes the termination handler; it does not resume the failed operation.
topics.question: What happens when an exception escapes a noexcept function?
steps: noexcept promises that no exception escapes the function.
An internally caught exception does not violate this promise.
If an exception escapes, the runtime invokes std::terminate.
An outer catch cannot be used to recover from that escaping exception in the usual way.
topics.mcq: An exception escaping a noexcept function calls:
options: The nearest ordinary outer catch normally
topics.explanation: A violated non-throwing specification invokes termination.

topics.subject: cia-2-2025-26:cpp
topics.title: unexpected() & bad_exception
topics.brief: These names appear in legacy exception-specification discussions. Learn the historical flow and label it clearly.
topics.hinglish: Ye old syllabus concepts hain; C++17 ke modern code mein unexpected() use mat karo.
points: Before C++17, dynamic specifications such as throw(int) restricted escaping exception types.
A violation called std::unexpected; its default handler called std::terminate.
A custom unexpected handler could throw an allowed type; under the old rules, bad_exception could substitute an otherwise disallowed exception if permitted.
Dynamic exception specifications and std::unexpected were removed in C++17. std::bad_exception itself still exists.
topics.question: Distinguish terminate(), unexpected() and bad_exception in the historical exception model.
steps: terminate ends execution when exception processing cannot continue.
Historically, unexpected responded to violation of a dynamic throw(type-list) specification.
The default unexpected handler terminated; special substitution rules could use bad_exception.
State the version boundary: dynamic specifications/unexpected removed in C++17; avoid using them in modern runnable examples.
topics.mcq: std::unexpected belongs mainly to:
topics.explanation: It was part of the old dynamic exception-specification mechanism.

topics.subject: cia-2-2025-26:cpp
topics.title: uncaught_exception() & standard classes
topics.brief: std::exception provides a standard base with what(). The old uncaught_exception boolean was replaced by a count-based facility.
topics.hinglish: what() error ka description deta hai. uncaught_exceptions() pending exceptions ki count deta hai.
points: Catch const std::exception& to handle many standard exception types.
what() returns an implementation-provided explanatory C-string for the exception.
uncaught_exception() returned a boolean; deprecated in C++17 and removed in C++20.
std::uncaught_exceptions(), available since C++17, returns the number of active uncaught exceptions.
topics.question: Explain std::exception, what() and the modern replacement for uncaught_exception().
steps: std::exception is the base of many standard exception classes.
Its virtual what() gives an explanatory message.
The singular uncaught_exception returned whether an exception was in flight.
The plural uncaught_exceptions returns a count, useful for detecting changes during stack unwinding.
topics.mcq: The return value of std::uncaught_exceptions() is:
topics.explanation: The plural function reports an integer count.

topics.subject: cia-2-2025-26:cpp
topics.title: OOP principles, classes, friends & scope
topics.brief: Objects combine state and behavior; access control separates a class interface from its implementation.
topics.hinglish: Encapsulation data aur methods ko organize karta hai; abstraction useful interface dikhata hai.
points: Classes support abstraction, encapsulation, inheritance and polymorphism; messages correspond to method calls.
class defaults to private access, struct to public; union members share storage.
Friend functions/classes receive declared access but are not automatically members; inline is not a guaranteed expansion command.
Use :: for qualified names. Nested/local classes have scope rules; static members belong to the class rather than each object.
topics.question: Explain encapsulation with a bank account interface.
steps: Keep balance private to stop arbitrary external changes.
Expose deposit and withdraw operations with validity checks.
Clients use these methods without depending on internal storage.
This bundles data/behavior and supports invariants; it does not by itself provide encryption or authentication.
topics.mcq: Default access inside class is:
topics.explanation: struct defaults to public; class defaults to private.

topics.subject: cia-2-2025-26:cpp
topics.title: Objects, references, this & pointers
topics.brief: An object can be passed by value, reference or pointer; the choice affects copying, mutation and lifetime.
topics.hinglish: const reference unnecessary copy avoid karta hai jab sirf read karna ho.
points: Passing by value copies/moves a value; const T& allows read-only access without that copy.
this points to the current object in a non-static member function.
Arrays of objects construct each element; pointer-to-member syntax differs from ordinary object pointers.
Object assignment updates an existing object; returning by value creates a result with copy elision/move opportunities.
topics.question: Compare void f(Box b), void f(Box& b), and void f(const Box& b).
steps: Box b creates a local value; modifications affect that copy.
Box& b refers to the caller’s object and allows modification.
const Box& b avoids the value copy but prevents mutation through that reference.
Choose based on ownership, size and whether the function should modify the caller.
topics.mcq: A non-static member’s this is:
topics.explanation: this identifies the instance whose member function is executing.

topics.subject: cia-2-2025-26:cpp
topics.title: Dynamic allocation & lifetime
topics.brief: new constructs dynamically allocated objects; delete destroys and releases them. Prefer ownership objects that clean up automatically.
topics.hinglish: new[] ke saath delete[]; mismatched cleanup undefined behavior ho sakta hai.
points: Match new with delete, new[] with delete[].
References must remain bound to live objects; dangling pointers/references are invalid to use.
For polymorphic deletion through a base pointer, the base needs a virtual destructor.
std::unique_ptr and standard containers manage ownership with RAII and reduce leaks.
topics.question: Identify the error in int* p=new int[5]; delete p;.
steps: new int[5] allocates an array.
delete p is the scalar deletion form.
The correct matching form is delete[] p.
Prefer std::vector<int> p(5) for automatic management in typical application code.
topics.mcq: The matching deallocation for new T[n] is:
topics.explanation: The array form must be matched.

topics.subject: cia-2-2025-26:cpp
topics.title: Overloading & constructors
topics.brief: Overloading provides multiple functions with the same name and different parameter lists. Constructors initialize objects.
topics.hinglish: Return type alone function overload distinguish nahi karta.
points: Overloads differ in parameter types/number; default arguments can create ambiguity.
Constructors may be default, parameterized or copy constructors; copy constructor convention is T(const T&).
An overloaded function address needs a target function-pointer type to select an overload.
A user-defined destructor/copy operation may require careful ownership handling; avoid shallow copies of owned raw resources.
topics.question: Why are f(int) and f(int,int=0) ambiguous when called as f(5)?
steps: Both functions accept one explicit integer argument.
The second uses its default for the omitted parameter.
Neither candidate is a better match for f(5).
Remove the conflicting default or redesign the overloads.
topics.mcq: Which is a conventional copy-constructor parameter?
topics.explanation: A reference avoids recursively copying while const permits copying const objects.

topics.subject: cia-2-2025-26:cpp
topics.title: Operator overloading & special operators
topics.brief: Operators can be defined for user-defined types while retaining their original precedence and arity.
topics.hinglish: Operator meaning sensible rakho; precedence redefine nahi hoti.
points: A member binary operator receives its right operand as a parameter; a non-member/friend receives both operands.
operator=, operator[], operator() and operator-> have special member-function rules.
Allocation/deallocation operators new/delete can be overloaded but must obey matching allocation contracts.
The comma operator can be overloaded, but ordinary comma sequencing intuition may be misleading; use clear interfaces.
topics.question: Show the idea of adding two Complex objects with a member operator+.
steps: Store real and imaginary parts in each object.
Define Complex operator+(const Complex& other) const.
Return a new object containing real+other.real and imag+other.imag.
Do not modify either operand; the result matches mathematical addition.
topics.mcq: Operator overloading can change:
options: The syntax of all built-in integers
topics.explanation: Arity and precedence remain fixed.

topics.subject: cia-2-2025-26:cpp
topics.title: Inheritance, access & virtual base classes
topics.brief: Inheritance creates relationships between base and derived types. Virtual inheritance shares a common base subobject in a diamond.
topics.hinglish: Virtual base diamond duplication solve karta hai; virtual function runtime dispatch karta hai—alag concepts.
points: Public inheritance preserves public/protected access categories; base private members remain inaccessible directly.
Multiple inheritance has several bases; qualify ambiguous member names or redesign the interface.
Construction runs base-to-derived; destruction runs derived-to-base.
A virtual base is constructed by the most-derived class and can prevent duplicate shared-base subobjects.
topics.recall: Construct bases first; destroy derived first
topics.question: Explain the diamond problem and the role of virtual inheritance.
steps: Suppose B and C inherit A, and D inherits both B and C.
Ordinary inheritance gives D two A subobjects, making A-member access ambiguous.
If B and C inherit A virtually, D shares one A subobject.
D initializes that virtual base; this solves duplication, not all possible naming/design ambiguities.
topics.mcq: Which class initializes a virtual base?
options: Only the compiler with no constructor
topics.explanation: Virtual-base initialization is the responsibility of the most-derived class.

topics.subject: cia-2-2025-26:cpp
topics.title: Virtual functions, abstract classes & RTTI
topics.brief: Virtual calls through pointers/references can dispatch to an overriding function in the actual derived object.
topics.hinglish: Base pointer, derived object: virtual method actual object ka call hota hai.
points: Early binding resolves statically; virtual calls support late binding.
A pure virtual function (=0) makes a class abstract unless all inherited pure functions are overridden.
Use override to catch signature mistakes; a polymorphic base commonly needs a virtual destructor.
dynamic_cast performs checked casts in polymorphic hierarchies: failed pointer cast gives nullptr, failed reference cast throws bad_cast. Know static_cast, const_cast and reinterpret_cast roles.
topics.question: What happens when Base* points to Derived and calls virtual show()?
steps: Determine the dynamic type of the pointed-to object: Derived.
Because show is virtual, dispatch uses that dynamic type.
Derived::show runs if it overrides the base function.
Without virtual, a call through Base* binds to the base version; passing by value can slice the object.
topics.mcq: A class with an unimplemented pure virtual function is:
topics.explanation: It cannot be directly instantiated.

topics.subject: cia-2-2025-26:cpp
topics.title: Streams & formatted I/O
topics.brief: C++ streams transport sequences of characters or bytes; manipulators control their formatting.
topics.hinglish: fixed ke saath setprecision decimal places control karta hai.
points: cin/cout are standard input/output streams; << inserts and >> extracts formatted data.
setw applies to the next formatted field; setfill chooses padding.
fixed plus setprecision(n) prints n digits after the decimal point for floating values.
Check stream state after input; invalid input may set failbit and leave later reads blocked until handled.
topics.question: Format 12.345 as a zero-padded width-8 field with two decimals.
steps: Use std::fixed and std::setprecision(2).
Rounding produces 12.35, five characters.
std::setw(8) requests three padding characters.
With std::setfill('0') and default right alignment, output is 00012.35.
topics.mcq: std::setw affects:
topics.explanation: Width is normally reset after formatted output.

topics.subject: cia-2-2025-26:cpp
topics.title: File classes, modes & error checks
topics.brief: ifstream reads, ofstream writes and fstream can do both. File modes determine how the file is opened.
topics.hinglish: app end par append karta hai; trunc existing content hata deta hai.
points: ios::in reads, out writes, app appends each write, binary disables text translation, trunc discards previous contents.
ios::ate starts at the end but still allows seeking elsewhere; it differs from app.
Check open success before using the stream and check bad/fail states appropriately.
Use while(getline(in,line)), not while(!in.eof()); opening an output file can overwrite content.
topics.question: Append one line to log.txt without truncating existing content.
steps: Construct ofstream with std::ios::app.
Check whether the stream opened successfully.
Write the line followed by a newline.
Check stream state after writing; report failure rather than silently claiming success.
topics.mcq: Which mode appends every write at the end?
topics.explanation: app enforces end-position writing.

topics.subject: cia-2-2025-26:cpp
topics.title: Namespaces, STL containers & iterators
topics.brief: Namespaces organize names; STL combines containers, iterators and algorithms.
topics.hinglish: Namespace collision solve karta hai. Iterator container ke elements traverse karta hai.
points: Qualify names with namespace::name; avoid broad using-directives in headers.
vector provides contiguous dynamic storage; list is a doubly linked sequence.
Iterators use begin/end; end is a past-the-end sentinel and must not be dereferenced.
Container mutations may invalidate iterators; the rules depend on container and operation.
topics.question: Traverse a vector with iterators and print every element.
steps: Construct vector<int> v{2,4,6}.
Initialize it=v.begin(), which refers to the first element.
While it!=v.end(), print *it and advance ++it.
Stop at end without dereferencing it. Output: 2 4 6.
topics.mcq: v.end() points to:
topics.explanation: The sentinel marks traversal completion.

topics.subject: cia-2-2025-26:cpp
topics.title: std::string operations
topics.brief: std::string owns a character sequence and provides search, replacement, comparison and substring operations.
topics.hinglish: find fail hone par npos return karta hai, −1 ko int mein assume mat karo.
points: compare returns negative, zero or positive for lexical ordering, not necessarily exactly −1 or +1.
swap exchanges contents; push_back appends one character; pop_back removes the last character of a nonempty string.
find returns the index or string::npos.
replace(pos,count,text) modifies a range; substr(pos,count) returns a new string.
topics.question: For s="exam prep", find and replace "prep" with "ready", then take the first four characters.
steps: s.find("prep") returns 5.
Check the result is not string::npos.
s.replace(5,4,"ready") gives "exam ready".
s.substr(0,4) returns "exam" without changing s.
topics.mcq: A failed std::string::find returns:
topics.explanation: npos is the documented not-found sentinel.
